# TwinGrid API reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_api_reference.py - do not edit by hand. -->

**Digital Twin API** - version `1.0.0`. Data centre digital twin simulation and optimization API.
The data behind these endpoints is **simulated**; nothing here is a measurement from a real facility.

Machine-readable contract: [`openapi.json`](openapi.json) (OpenAPI 3.1.0). The running API also serves it at `/openapi.json`, with Swagger UI at `/docs` and ReDoc at `/redoc`.

Regenerate after any route change: `python scripts/gen_api_reference.py`. A test (`tests/test_task9_api_reference.py`) fails when these files are stale.

## Authentication

- `POST /auth/login` returns an access token (short-lived JWT) and a refresh token; send the access token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- `POST /auth/refresh` rotates the refresh token; `POST /auth/logout` revokes it.
- Roles: `viewer` (default) and `operator`. Endpoints marked `role operator` answer 403 to a viewer.
- Routes with auth `none` need no token (login, register, probes).
- `/ws/live` (WebSocket, not part of OpenAPI) accepts a one-time ticket from `POST /auth/ws-ticket`; a `?token=` query token is accepted only while `WS_ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN` is not `false`.
- See `SECURITY.md` for the token lifecycle.

## Rate-limit classes

Every HTTP route is in the `general` window; a route that names a class is also in that class. Windows are sliding, per user (valid token) or per client IP, in memory per process. Over the limit -> `429` with `Retry-After`. Probes (`/livez`, `/readyz`, `/healthz`) are exempt. `/auth/*` routes additionally have a per-IP limit from `slowapi`. Defaults below; each is overridable by the environment variable shown.

| Class | Default | Environment variable |
|---|---|---|
| `alert_ack` | 30/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_ALERT_ACK` |
| `anomaly_score` | 30/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_ANOMALY_SCORE` |
| `benchmark` | 30/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_BENCHMARK` |
| `esg_report` | 6/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_ESG_REPORT` |
| `general` | 120/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_GENERAL` |
| `optimize` | 10/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_OPTIMIZE` |
| `shadow_sample` | 10/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_SHADOW_SAMPLE` |
| `simulate` | 6/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_SIMULATE` |
| `state` | 30/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_STATE` |
| `telemetry_read` | 60/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_TELEMETRY_READ` |
| `train_async` | 5/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_TRAIN_ASYNC` |
| `webhook` | 30/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_WEBHOOK` |
| `whatif` | 30/minute | `RATE_LIMIT_WHATIF` |

Compute-heavy routes are also bounded in concurrency and wall-clock time: `429 compute_busy` when too many run at once, `504 compute_timeout` when one runs too long.

## Error shape

Every failure is `application/problem+json`:

```json
{
  "type": "urn:twingrid:error:<code>",
  "title": "Not Found",
  "status": 404,
  "detail": "<one-line human message, always a string>",
  "instance": "/request/path",
  "request_id": "<same value as the X-Request-ID response header>",
  "errors": [{"loc": ["query", "hours"], "msg": "...", "type": "..."}]
}
```

- `errors` appears on `422` only; each item is `{loc, msg, type}` (the caller's raw input is never echoed).
- `instance` is the path only, never the query string.
- An unhandled server error is a generic `500` (`Internal server error`); tracebacks, file paths and SQL never reach the client.
